problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{3}{13}($
{{field-1}} $)$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{3x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{e}^{3x}, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{3x})(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))-\int (\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))(3{e}^{3x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-\frac{3}{2}J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{3x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{e}^{3x}, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{3x})(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))-\int (-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))(3{e}^{3x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{3}{2}I.\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-\frac{3}{2}J \\ I & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-\frac{3}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{3}{2}I) \\ I & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)-\frac{9}{4}I \\ \frac{13}{4}I & ={e}^{3x}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)) \\ I & =\frac{1}{13}{e}^{3x}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =(\frac{1}{13}{e}^{3x}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{13}{e}^{3(\pi /2)}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )))-(\frac{1}{13}{e}^{3(0)}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}{e}^{3\pi /2}(2\cdot 0+3\cdot (-1))-\frac{3}{13} \\  & =-\frac{3}{13}({e}^{3\pi /2}+1)\end{aligned}
$$
